title: Exactness of the canonical module section boundary
statement: Let $X$ be a ringed space and $S:0\to A\to B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ a short exact sequence of its module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Use module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] and the canonical connecting map [def-sc-module-cohomology-boundary], computed in any chosen derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define the section boundary $\Gamma(X,C)\to H^1(X,A)$ as the canonical degree-zero comparison $\Gamma(X,C)\simeq H^0(X,C)$ followed by that connecting map. For every $s\in\Gamma(X,C)$ its section boundary is zero if and only if there exists $t\in\Gamma(X,B)$ with $\Gamma(g)(t)=s$.

source.place: Tag 01DZ, cohomology as right-derived global sections and its long exact sequence; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01DZ

proof.text: Apply derived global sections to the canonical distinguished triangle of a short exact module sequence. It remains distinguished; the derived homology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] is exact at degree zero of the quotient. Transport its maps by the canonical single-complex comparison defining [def-sc-module-cohomology-boundary].

proof.text: Global sections preserves finite limits, so its map to the zeroth derived functor is an isomorphism. Naturality identifies the quotient map after this comparison. In a module category exactness says that the kernel of the second map is the image of the first; evaluating this equality on s gives the desired equivalence with existence of a lifting global section.
